headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance gaps are plausible but undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads files and runs browsers; Agent B reads and writes the filesystem and executes shell commands. If A’s research outputs or downloaded content are placed in B’s workspace, B can ingest attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance or isolation, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Agent A writes web-derived content into a shared directory that Agent B later parses
IF Agent B treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B
Disable automatic parsing of A-generated files by B
Add a provenance header check before B consumes files
Use read-only handoff files between agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles local documents, citations, and images and has broad network egress; Agent B handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files and can write files. A shared workspace or handoff path could expose sensitive research material or model artifacts to the other agent, and A’s egress increases exfiltration risk. No isolation is documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or mounted volume
IF Agent A uploads file contents from shared files to external APIs
IF Agent B writes logs or outputs containing A’s sensitive inputs
mitigations: Use separate encrypted workspaces
Restrict A’s uploads to approved sources only
Redact secrets before any file handoff
Rotate and scope API keys per agent
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A can install packages, read files, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; Agent B can execute shell, install packages, read/write files, and spawn subprocesses. Both can mutate the same local environment, so concurrent runs can overwrite dependencies, configs, or outputs. No locking or shared-state controls are documented, making default overlap dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same filesystem or Python environment
IF package installation or file writes occur concurrently
IF shared configuration or output directories are used
mitigations: Run each agent in its own container
Use separate virtual environments
Serialize package installation steps
Mount shared paths read-only
requires-engineering: add file locks and workspace arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A is a research/content-writing agent that produces reports and citations; Agent B is a support/training agent that can act on files and shell commands. If B consumes A’s outputs as authoritative, any hallucination or malformed citation from A can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or published artifacts. No verification step is documented between them.
conditions: IF Agent B uses Agent A’s report or citations as input without independent verification
IF B performs shell actions or file updates based on A’s generated text
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A outputs
Add a verification pass against source documents
Limit B to read-only consumption of A outputs
Log source-to-output traceability
requires-engineering: implement structured validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A touches research queries, local documents, citations, and images and uses third-party APIs; Agent B touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data and calls external model services. The pair could mix data classes with different retention or residency expectations, but the profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch. Uncertainty therefore stays at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is processed by both agents in the same workflow
IF external APIs retain prompts, files, or logs beyond the operator’s policy
IF residency or retention requirements differ between the two toolchains
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Block regulated data from external APIs
Set explicit retention limits on logs and outputs
Document jurisdiction and vendor terms for each API
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit trails
